notes: Only DenseMatrix parallel zero initialization is retained in the solver. Public initialization semantics, tolerances, and applicable exact certificates are unchanged.
Overwrite allocation and globally replacing zero memset with AVX-512 or rep stosb were rejected. Their complete solve results and correctness evaluations are retained.

The large initialization path uses arithmetic elements except bool, >= 4 MiB buffers, and assigns disjoint 2 MiB-aligned address regions to OpenMP workers. Small matrices and class types use serial value initialization.
Wall sampling and memset traces diagnose the leader thread, not aggregate CPU or worker cost. Performance conclusions use unsampled fresh-process end-to-end comparisons.

The broad batch is one pair per case for screening, not a speedup claim. Five cases exceeding 3% slowdown were repeated seven times; halfslab was repeated 15 times and then 31 times with no concurrent build/evaluation. All batches remain visible.
The final hsolve binary is hash-identical to the full-test and performance candidate. The final polish only changes metadata/documentation and excludes bool from the arithmetic branch.
The cavity SLEPc comparison reuses p12_compare.py and its P12 metadata label; the actual hsolve-p15 binary is archived and hash-identified here.

The million-row comparison uses the current MPI binary versus the previously validated SLEPc profile, on the same gpu02 host and two-socket 16-core allocation. There is no archived pre-P15 MPI binary, so this is not a P15 before/after comparison.
No claim is made that all open-source implementations or all workloads have been beaten.
